name: Omer
overview: The omer is a biblical dry measure defined as one-tenth of an ephah, used in the context of gathering manna as commanded by the LORD to the Israelites (Exodus 16:16, 36). The amount gathered by each person was measured by the omer, ensuring equitable provision with none left over or lacking (Exodus 16:17-18). Rabbinic tradition estimates the omer at about two quarts, while Josephus records it as three and one-half quarts, highlighting slight variations in historical understanding of this measure.
